title: Mortgage Rates Edge Back Up to 6.66%; 15-Year at 5.98%, Jumbo Eases to ~6.71%
summary: Freddie Mac's Aug. 27 Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.66%, one basis point above the prior week and up from 6.56% a year ago, snapping a two-week slide. The 15-year averaged 5.98%, up from 5.95%. Chief economist Sam Khater cited resilient consumer spending and rising household incomes, with more listings and slower price growth giving buyers better options and creating a more balanced market. The 30-year jumbo average moved the other way, easing roughly eight basis points on the week to about 6.71%, narrowing the jumbo-to-conforming spread to about five basis points.

title: Fairfield Buys West Palm Beach's 812-Unit Portofino Place From Cortland for $208M at ~$256,200 Per Door
summary: San Diego-based Fairfield Residential paid $208 million for the 812-unit Portofino Place Apartments at 4400 and 4600 Portofino Way in West Palm Beach, buying from Atlanta-based Cortland - about $256,200 per unit and the second-largest South Florida multifamily trade of the year. The 2003- and 2006-built complex spans 34 three-story buildings and two clubhouses on nearly 40 acres; Fairfield financed it with $93.1 million and $85 million Freddie Mac loans maturing in 2033. South Florida multifamily investment volume reached $2.5 billion in the first half, up 19.4% year over year per Avison Young, and in the 12 months through Q2 leasing (13,774 units) outpaced deliveries (12,751) for the first time in three years per CoStar - though average asking rents still slipped 1.3% year over year to $2,279 in July.

title: Midtown Capital Pays $86M for 14-Building Doral Industrial Portfolio at $296 PSF; Mana Wynwood Sale to Ken Griffin Reported at $700M-Plus
summary: Midtown Capital Partners acquired a 300,000-square-foot, 14-property small-bay industrial portfolio along Northwest 54th and 56th Streets and Northwest 79th and 82nd Avenues in Doral for $86 million - roughly $296 per square foot and a near-record for Miami-Dade - from 13 separate sellers tied to the Waas family, who developed and managed the buildings for decades. Miami industrial posted 402,000 square feet of positive net absorption in the second quarter, pulling vacancy to 6.9% with rents near record highs, per Avison Young. Separately, The Real Deal reports that Moishe Mana's 30-acre Mana Wynwood campus is being sold to billionaire Ken Griffin at a rumored $700 million to more than $1 billion, which would set a South Florida record for a development assemblage; neither party has confirmed the deal, and both denied it earlier this year.

title: Lost Tree Village Waterfront Teardown Trades for $27.5M - More Than $4,000 Per Foot in North Palm Beach
summary: The estate of the late Penn Corporation founder Dana Hamel sold 11800 Turtle Beach Road in North Palm Beach for $27.5 million, over $4,000 per square foot on a 6,800-square-foot home built in 1992. The property listed in April at $35 million; Hamel had paid $2.5 million for it in 1991. The buyer, shielded behind 11800 Turtle Beach Rd LLC, plans to tear down and rebuild on the roughly one-acre lot with 128 feet of water frontage. James Kenny and Paul Kaneb of K2 Realty had the listing and represented both sides. Lost Tree Village, a 450-acre community with a private oceanfront and golf course, set its record at $55 million last year.

title: Amendment 3 Would Lift Florida's Homestead Exemption to $250K and Cut $11.86B a Year From Local Tax Rolls
summary: The November ballot measure would raise Florida's homestead exemption from $50,000 today to $150,000 next year and $250,000 by 2028 for non-school property taxes, and halve the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead property — investment homes, second homes and commercial real estate — from 10% to 5%. State economists put the statewide revenue hit at $11.86 billion a year, with Miami-Dade losing an estimated $445 million and Broward $326 million annually by fiscal 2028-29. Three consolidated lawsuits forced a court-ordered rewrite of the ballot language, and University of North Florida polling showed support sliding from 61% to 45% once voters were told the budget impact — well under the 60% threshold required to pass.

title: 25-Story Live Local Act Tower Filed in Downtown West Palm Beach — 40% Workforce Housing, 60% Condos
summary: Urban Design Studio and Arquitectonica submitted a pre-application for a 25-story tower at 215 Fifth Street in downtown West Palm Beach: 36 workforce-housing rentals on the second and third floors and 41 market-rate condos above, including an 8,500-square-foot penthouse, with a fourth-floor amenity deck and pool. The developer has not been identified; the vacant 1920s commercial site last sold in 2005 for $5.9 million to an entity tied to Marsha Stocker, daughter of the late Palm Beach landlord Burt Handelsman. The Live Local Act, signed in 2023 and expanded this year, grants tax breaks and lets developers bypass municipal approval when at least 40% of units are workforce or affordable. Steve Ross and Jeff Greene have both filed Live Local projects nearby.

title: Whole Foods-Anchored Doral Marketplace Trades for $83M at $1,056 Per Square Foot
summary: An entity managed by Jonathan Perlman, founder and CEO of Dallas-based Tradition Senior Living, bought the newly completed 78,600-square-foot Doral Marketplace at Northwest 41st Street and Northwest 107th Avenue from Atlanta-based SJC Ventures, assuming the seller's $50.1 million loan, which was reassigned to Bank of Texas. The 8.2-acre center holds a 38,000-square-foot Whole Foods plus 40,700 square feet of strip retail and 488 parking spaces. SJC and Nuveen paid $32 million for the site in 2024 and delivered the project this year. Grocery-anchored retail keeps clearing steadily in South Florida: Nuveen paid $46.3 million for Aldi-anchored Coral Landings III in Margate in April, and Publix bought Fountains of Boynton for $78 million in May.

title: Una Residences Penthouse Sells for $17.9M at $2,700 PSF; Key Biscayne Waterfront Trades at $3,300 PSF
summary: A trust paid $17.9 million for a 6,200-square-foot penthouse at Una Residences, 175 Southeast 25th Road in Brickell, developed by OKO Group and Cain — $2,700 per square foot and the day's priciest recorded South Florida home sale. In Key Biscayne, 591 North Mashta Drive sold for $14.3 million, or $3,300 per square foot, from a company managed by Alvaro Castro Mendivil to Isabela Ribaudo; the 4,300-square-foot house last traded at $3.2 million in 2004 and was asking just under $17 million in January (Cristina Anglemont De Tassigny of EXP Realty had the listing, Giulietta Ulloa of BHHS EWM Realty brought the buyer). A three-bedroom at Five Park, 501 West Avenue in Miami Beach, fetched $8.5 million, or $3,400 per square foot, up from $7 million in 2024.

title: Palm Beach Billionaires' Row Estate Lists for $195M — A Sale at Ask Would Set an Island Record
summary: A rebuilt-from-scratch lake-to-ocean estate at 1616 South Ocean Boulevard hit the market at $195 million, roughly $9,790 per square foot. The nearly 20,000-square-foot, 7-bedroom/12.5-bath home sits on almost two acres with both Intracoastal and Atlantic frontage and an 18-car garage; it was reconstructed in 2023. Christian Angle Real Estate has the listing. The property last traded at $22.4 million in 2018 and was owned by former Avis CEO Joseph Vittoria, who paid about $5.7 million in 1996. A sale at ask would eclipse the island's $170 million record set in 2023 at 589 North County Road. Angle also holds a $205 million former Gucci-heir compound, and a 2.25-acre estate at 911 North Ocean Boulevard has been asking $185 million since November.

title: Design District Commercial Condo Trades for $17.3M at $680 PSF; Miami Industrial and Palm Springs School Also Close
summary: Alta Developers sold a 25,500-square-foot commercial condo at the Quadro, 3900 Biscayne Boulevard in Miami's Design District, for $17.3 million — about $680 per square foot — to Hollywood-based JBL Asset Management; Alta completed the 12-story project in 2019. Also recorded: a 10,300-square-foot industrial complex at 6400 Northwest 84th Avenue in Miami for $6.5 million, sold by an Alan Leibowitz entity to an affiliate of Roberts Oxygen Company after trading at $4.8 million in 2024; and the 9,900-square-foot Kingswood Academy early-childhood center at 4137 South Congress Avenue in Palm Springs for just under $6 million on a 2.4-acre lot.

title: Apartment Property Insurance Up 58% in Five Years — The Fastest-Growing Landlord Expense, Trepp Finds
summary: Property insurance has climbed 58 percent over the past five years, making it the fastest-growing major operating-expense line for apartment owners, according to new research from Trepp cited by The Real Deal. With rent growth decelerating, the increase lands directly on net operating income — and on the cap rates buyers are willing to underwrite. The pressure is sharpest in coastal Florida, where premiums have run well above national averages, though Citizens' 2026 rate reductions and softer reinsurance pricing have begun to ease the trend on the residential side.

title: Palm Beach Lakefront Estate Sells for $26.5M - 1,458% Above Its 2005 Price
summary: A lakefront house at 127 Ocean View Road in Palm Beach's Estate Section, about a mile south of Mar-a-Lago, traded for a recorded $26.5 million after more than 25 years in the same family. Heidi Niblack and retired pharmaceutical executive John Niblack sold as co-trustees of a revocable trust; the buyer was Florida Iconic Ventures LLC, managed by Issac Ashkenazy and sharing an address with New York-based Ashkenazy Acquisition Corp. The 1999-built, four-bedroom house has 8,387 square feet inside and out plus a lakefront pool and spa. The sellers paid $1.7 million in 2005 for the house and an oceanfront parcel down the street - a 1,458% gain.
source: Palm Beach Daily News via Boca Raton Tribune

title: Miami Beach Double-Lot Mansion Trades for $51.5M; Al Capone's Former Palm Island Lot Fetches $21M
summary: A trust paid $51.5 million for the newly built waterfront mansion at 270 South Hibiscus Drive in Miami Beach, off a $55 million ask. The seller was an entity managed by broker Denis Smykalov; the 10,500-square-foot, seven-bedroom house sits on a double lot. Jordan Karp had the listing and Dora Puig of Luxe Living Realty represented the buyer. Separately, the 30,000-square-foot waterfront lot at 93 Palm Avenue that once held Al Capone's mansion sold for $21 million to an LLC tied to Russian businessman Ilya Karpov, up from $15.5 million in 2021.

title: Brickell Development Site Sells for $50M for Planned 60-Story Tower; SW Miami-Dade Industrial Trades at $24.5M
summary: Prosper Group and Versluys Group paid $50 million for a Brickell assemblage - two commercial buildings totaling 16,800 square feet at 625 SW First Avenue and 66 SW Sixth Street plus a 74,400-square-foot vacant lot at 99 SW Seventh Street - from Two Roads Development and Newgard Development Group. The buyers are planning a 60-story residential tower on the site. In southwest Miami-Dade, a 155,000-square-foot two-story industrial building and parking lot at 11900-11905 SW 128th Street changed hands for $24.5 million.

title: Mortgage Rates Fall a Second Straight Week to 6.65%; 15-Year Dips to 5.95%
summary: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.65% for the week ending August 20, down from 6.67% and the second consecutive weekly decline. The 15-year fixed eased to 5.95% from 5.96%. Both sit modestly above year-ago levels of 6.58% and 5.69%. Jumbo 30-year pricing averaged roughly 6.78%, down from about 6.84% in mid-August - the more relevant benchmark for most South Florida coastal and luxury purchases, where loan sizes clear the $832,750 conforming ceiling.

title: Russian Businessman Sells Miami Beach's 2740 North Bay Road Lot for $72M, More Than Triple His 2022 Price
summary: Ilyha Karpov sold the vacant 0.6-acre waterfront lot at 2740 North Bay Road in Miami Beach to a trust for $72 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida residential deal. Karpov had paid $20.8 million for the site in 2022, buying from Delphine Dray, owner of Miami Beach's National Hotel. The top commercial trade was in Miami Beach as well: an affiliate of Coral Gables-based Capital Realty Services sold the 31,000 SF two-story mixed-use building at 1200 Washington Avenue for $10 million, or about $323 per square foot, to an entity managed by investor Ryan Manoocheri; the property last traded for $2.8 million more than two decades ago. Also recorded: the estate of Rudolf Silk sold a 42,000 SF West Palm Beach industrial property at 2658-2660 Electronics Way for $7.8 million, and John Thomas Hayes paid $6.2 million for a 2022-built waterfront home at 3701 Northeast 26th Avenue in Lighthouse Point.
